subject: Hosted evaluation - quickstart access, concurrency & endpoint plan
messages:
From: Avery Collins <avery@paydrift.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-24T13:02:00Z
Subject: Follow-up: Hosted trial questions after demo

Thanks again for the demo earlier. PayDrift is excited — we liked the low-latency demo and the KV caching example. Before we commit to a short hosted trial we have a few technical questions to validate fit: 

- Sustained concurrency: what's a realistic sustained concurrent requests per second we can expect on the hosted tier for a 7B vs 70B model? Any guidance on per-connection/worker concurrency we should architect for?
- Cold-start/caching behavior: how long does the platform keep model instances warm for low-traffic prefixes? Does the prefix/KV cache persist across identical requests in different endpoints?
- Burst capacity & throttling: we need to understand burst behavior (30s-2m spikes) and what rate-limit responses look like (429 body shapes, retry-after semantics).
- Quickstart sandbox: can we get sandbox credentials with two endpoints (staging & canary) and a temporary higher rate window for an initial PoC?

Mostly looking for concrete numbers so our SREs can size our front-end backoff and retry logic. Happy to hop back on a short call if that's easier.

—Avery
Avery Collins
Sr. PM, PayDrift

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Avery Collins <avery@paydrift.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-24T14:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Hosted trial questions after demo

Hi Avery — great to hear PayDrift is interested, and excellent questions. Summary of what I captured on the call + proposed next steps below.

Highlights / quick answers
- Sustained concurrency: for hosted evals we usually recommend planning for 20–50 concurrent active requests for a 7B-like profile, and 8–16 for larger 70B-class models for consistent 95th/99th p99 latencies in the single-digit-second range. We’ll provide more precise numbers after we profile your prompt lengths.
- Cold starts & cache: our runtime keeps hot workers for ~5–10 minutes under light traffic; prefix/KV caching is per-customer and will be available across endpoints in the same sandbox unless you request isolation.
- Burst & throttling: default hosted behavior returns 429 with a standard Retry-After header; we can provide a temporary burst window for PoC (details below).

Immediate next steps (what I’ll coordinate):
1) Provision sandbox access (staging + canary) for PayDrift with two endpoints: /v1/generate-staging and /v1/generate-canary. Token and key details included in the checklist (attached).
2) Temporary trial rate profile: enable a 20% higher burst allowance for the first 72 hours of the PoC and a recommended baseline per-minute rate.
3) Technical sync: quick 30-minute alignment with your SREs to capture prompt length distribution and expected concurrency so we can tune worker counts.

Can you confirm a 30-minute window tomorrow (2026-06-25) at 10:00am PT? If that works I’ll loop in our infra lead (Karthik) and CS (Monica) so we can lock down the sandbox defaults.

Attaching: redwood_quickstart-checklist.pdf and a CSV with proposed sandbox endpoints and initial rate numbers.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
T: +1 (415) 555-0142
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Avery Collins <avery@paydrift.com>
Date: 2026-06-24T15:05:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Follow-up: Hosted trial questions after demo — need sandbox defaults

Hi team — forwarding PayDrift's follow-up (below). They want concrete numbers to size their front-end. Can you confirm suggestions for the hosted trial sandbox? Key asks:

- Baseline per-minute rate (tokens/min or requests/min) we should provision for staging and canary endpoints during PoC.
- Burst rules: how to configure temporary 72-hour burst window and what guardrails to enforce to avoid noisy-neighbor impact.
- Concurrency guidance: recommended worker concurrency per model family (7B / 70B) and whether we should pin to a specific model variant for the trial.
- KV cache TTL and whether cross-endpoint cache sharing is safe by default.

Suggested defaults (please edit):
* Staging endpoint: 120 requests/minute, 600k tokens/min burst cap for 72h (auto-roll to baseline after window)
* Canary endpoint: 30 requests/minute, 150k tokens/min burst
* Worker concurrency: 32 for 7B, 10 for 70B (per instance)
* KV cache TTL: 24h; shared within sandbox by default

If you can confirm or adjust by EOD I’ll push these back to PayDrift and provision the keys.

Thanks — tessa
